mx-three-guarantees.title: Flag of the Three Guarantees
desc:
- The Flag of the Three Guarantees (1821) was Mexico's first national flag, featuring diagonal stripes of green, white, and red with a crowned eagle on a cactus in the centre and three stars
- The three guarantees were: independence from Spain, Roman Catholic religion, and union of all inhabitants
- These were the principles of the Plan of Iguala that secured Mexican independence
- **Construction:** three diagonal stripes of white (top-left to bottom-right), green (behind), and red (front)
- Three six-pointed stars in each stripe
- A crowned eagle on a cactus centred
- Ratio approximately 4:7
trivia:
- The flag of the Army of Three Guarantees represented Mexico's independence movement
- The three guarantees were religion, independence, and union
- Led to Mexico's independence from Spain in 1821

mx-empire.title: Flag of the First Mexican Empire
desc:
- The flag of the Mexican Empire (1821–1823 and 1864–1867) used the green-white-red vertical tricolour with the imperial coat of arms — an eagle with an imperial crown
- The First Mexican Empire under Agustín de Iturbide and the Second under Emperor Maximilian I both used variations of this imperial flag before their respective collapses
- **Construction:** three equal vertical bands of green (hoist), white, and red
- The imperial eagle with crown is centred on the white band
- Ratio approximately 4:7
trivia:
- The Mexican Empire (1821–1823) was a brief empire after independence
- The emperor was Agustín de Iturbide
- Replaced by the Mexican Republic

mx-federal-republic.title: Flag of the Mexican Federal Republic
desc: - The Mexican Federal Republic (1823–1864) replaced the crown with a republican eagle and serpent on the tricolour — establishing the design used to this day
- **Construction:** three equal vertical bands of green, white, and red with an eagle-on-cactus emblem (without the later additions of laurel and oak branches)
trivia:
- The First Mexican Federal Republic (1824–1835) represented early Mexican democracy
- Adopted a federal system inspired by the United States
- Later replaced by centralist governments
